note: NOT BANKED. Stage-1 test slice, authored to be attacked. Per the pre-registration a failed slice is discarded, never banked, and never tuned item-by-item against its own attack. Each distractor records the near-miss line it is the correct reply to; that field is authoring provenance and must never enter study_item_bank.item.
revision: Second pass. The first was rejected by its own pre-flight: the key was the longest option in 11/12 and carried a question mark in 11/12 against 53% for distractors. Cause: the keys engaged a two-part constraint while the near-miss lines were simple, so their replies ran short and flat. Fixed by giving each near-miss line its own complication and by letting the key state rather than ask in 5 of 12.

items.line: The reading list went up last night, but the library only has the second edition and the seminar's on the third.
choices: The numbering won't match, then. I'll use the library copy and check page references later.
Then buying one is the only way. Does the campus shop keep it, or would it be an order?
I'll watch for it going up — they usually post the list a fortnight ahead, don't they?
I hadn't heard it had been moved at all. Is the new time on the department page, or by email?
nearMiss: the library doesn't have the book at all
the reading list hasn't gone up yet
the seminar has been rescheduled

items.line: I've got the studio booked for Thursday, but it's the small one, so there isn't room for the whole ensemble.
choices: Thursday's awkward for me this week. Is the Friday slot still going spare?
We'd have to split the rehearsal across two sessions, then. Strings first, or winds?
None of them free at all? We could ask about the chapel, though it's cold.
That's ample for the six of us, surely. Shall I tell the others Thursday?
nearMiss: the studio is booked but on a different day
no studio could be booked at all
the ensemble is a small one

items.line: Professor Nadel's office hours have moved to Monday, though she's away at a conference all next week.
choices: Monday suits me better anyway. I'll go along at the usual time and hope it's quiet.
I'll wait until she's back from it. Her hours are normally Thursdays, aren't they?
The first Monday I could catch her is the week after, then. I'll email instead.
She's back in time for the Monday, then? I'll try to catch her first thing that morning.
nearMiss: the hours moved and she is around
she is away and the hours are unchanged
the conference is this week rather than next

items.line: The grant covers travel but not accommodation, and the conference hotel is the only one within an hour.
choices: Then it's the fare I need to budget for. Do they reimburse advance tickets?
That's better than I'd expected, then. I'll get the hotel booked today and claim it back.
I'll look at somewhere further out. How far is reasonable to commute each morning?
We're out of pocket either way, then. Any chance of sharing a room to halve it?
nearMiss: the grant covers accommodation but not travel
the grant covers both
there are other hotels nearby

items.line: They've put the submission deadline back a week, but the marking still has to be in by the same date.
choices: That takes the pressure off both ends, then. I'll stop worrying about the schedule.
So the turnaround gets shorter, not longer. Does that mean briefer comments?
Do we know yet whether the marking date shifts as well, or is that still open?
A week earlier than planned? That's going to be very tight for the final chapter.
nearMiss: both the deadline and the marking date moved
the deadline moved and the marking date was not mentioned
the deadline was brought forward

items.line: The rail replacement bus runs on the hour, and the last one goes before the lecture finishes.
choices: Then I've a comfortable margin after all. I'll take the one at ten.
Nothing running at all this weekend? I'd better see about sharing a taxi back.
It finishes at eight, doesn't it? That should just about work, then.
It's leave early or find another way back, then. I'll look at the trains.
nearMiss: the last bus goes after the lecture finishes
there is no replacement service
the lecture finishes earlier than stated

items.line: I can mark your draft this week, but only if it's the full chapter — I can't judge the argument from one section.
choices: I'll hold it back till Friday and send the whole chapter rather than half of it now.
I'll send what I've got tonight and the rest once it's finished.
Next week is fine by me. Shall I aim for the Monday?
I'll pull out the middle section, then — that's the part I'm least sure of.
nearMiss: any portion is welcome
this week is not possible
a single section is what is wanted

items.line: The department will pay for the licence, but it's charged per machine, and you work on both the lab desktop and your laptop.
choices: Simple enough, then. I'll put it on both and get on with the analysis.
I'll see whether there's a student rate before I give up on it entirely.
It's two licences or one machine, then. Which comes cheaper for them?
I'll do that work in the lab, then, and leave the laptop out of it.
nearMiss: the licence is charged per user
the department will not pay
only lab machines are covered

items.line: Your supervisor has signed the form, but the graduate office wants a second signature, and the head of department is away till Monday.
choices: I'll catch him tomorrow, then, and get it in with time to spare.
I'll chase her for the signature first and worry about the rest afterwards.
No rush on it at all, then. I'll sort it out once he's back.
It can't go in before Friday unless someone deputises. Is anyone acting?
nearMiss: the head of department is available
the supervisor has not signed yet
there is no deadline on the form

items.line: The archive will let you photograph the loose letters but not the bound volumes, and most of what you're after is bound.
choices: It's transcribing by hand for the bulk of it, then. I'll allow extra days.
That'll save me days of work. I'll bring the camera along on Tuesday.
Not even the loose material, then? It's notebooks the whole way through, in that case.
Then I can photograph nearly all of it. That's a considerable relief.
nearMiss: photography is allowed throughout
no photography is allowed at all
most of the material is loose

items.line: I've put you down for the Tuesday tutorial, though you'd said Thursdays were better — Tuesday was the only one with a space.
choices: Thursday, then, if it's going spare. That fits round the lab far better.
Nothing at all this term? I'll ask about sitting in unofficially.
I'll take it rather than lose the place. Is there a list if someone drops out?
Tuesday's ideal, thanks. That's the one I'd have picked myself.
nearMiss: both days had spaces
neither day had a space
Tuesday was the stated preference

items.line: The results came back consistent, but the control ran at a different temperature, so we can't publish them as they stand.
choices: Then we can start writing up. Shall I draft the methods section?
It's a rerun of the control, not the whole set. How long would that take?
Inconsistent how — between replicates, or against the earlier run?
Then the whole batch is compromised and we'd have to start again from scratch.
nearMiss: everything ran as intended
the results came back inconsistent
the samples, not the control, ran at the wrong temperature
